Subject: Post-call recap: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private — residency constraints + proposed next steps

Hi Carlos / Elenia,

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap from our call and recommended next steps so your procurement and security teams have something to work from. I summarized the main constraints you called out and our recommended paths: 

Summary (what we heard)
- Primary requirement: all production customer data must remain in the EU for at-rest and in-transit processing.
- Secondary requirement: disaster recovery / cold backups may be stored in APAC if encrypted and KMS keys are controlled by FinTrust.
- Latency target: EU users should see token-latency ~<100ms for typical prompt sizes.
- Procurement preference: minimize custom on-prem work but willing to consider Dedicated or Private if Hosted cannot meet residency/SLA requirements.

Recommended options (high level)
1) Hosted API (EU-only region): fastest path to production. We can pin model version and route all inference and KV caching to eu-west-1. Meets EU residency for active traffic; supports KMS integration for customer-managed keys.
2) Redwood Dedicated (EU reserved capacity): if you need guaranteed throughput and an SLA-backed latency target, Dedicated pools can be provisioned in the EU and isolated to your tenant. Good fit if procurement requires committed capacity.
3) Private VPC / On-prem: for the strictest controls (air-gapped or specific network/topology), our Private deployment places the control plane in your VPC and supports HSM/KMS integrations. This is the heavier lift and typically for regulated workloads that can’t accept any cross-region failover.

Routing / failover note
- Cross-region failover (EU -> APAC or EU -> US) is technically supported as a fallback but has compliance implications: if the contract requires EU-only processing at all times, automated cross-region failover would violate that. We can implement manual failover or region-constrained fallbacks that only engage under documented emergency scenarios with approvals.

Attachments: I attached a lightweight residency matrix and an architecture sketch showing Hosted vs Dedicated options.
[Attachment: residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)]
[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-arch.png (image)]

Next steps I suggest:
- Technical deep-dive with your security/procurement + our solutions engineer (Neha) to map to your checklist (30–45 min) — propose Tue 13 Oct, 10:00 CET.
- Neha to share a short note on KMS/HSM options and what changes between Hosted and Private.
- Prep a mutual action plan (MAP) and high-level timeline if you want us to scope a Dedicated sizing exercise.

Carlos / Elenia — please confirm who from procurement/security should join the technical call and whether the DR backups in APAC (encrypted, customer KMS) would be acceptable as a ‘secondary’ storage location.

Thanks,
Priyom

Hi Carlos / Elenia — quick technical clarifications to the questions above.

1) Hosted EU-only configuration
- We can constrain all inference traffic, model storage, and KV cache to an EU region (eu-west-1). Logging can also be routed to an EU-only logging destination. We support customer-managed KMS; if you bring your own key we can ensure encryption using your key in the EU.
- Caveat: features like centralized cross-region analytics (optional) would be disabled for compliance.

2) Backups in APAC under customer KMS
- Backups are supported cross-region with encrypted blobs. If the contract allows DR backups in APAC with customer KMS keys that are EU-originated and controlled, we can model that as a compliant scenario, but procurement/legal must sign off. For the strictest interpretation of ‘EU-only processing at all times’, backups in APAC present a compliance risk.

3) Latency benchmarks
- Hosted eu-west-1: median token latency for small prompts ~70–90ms (varies by model family and prompt size).
- Dedicated EU pool: optimized kernels and reserved capacity can reduce p95 latency by ~10–20% vs noisy multi-tenant Hosted. We can run a short benchmark with your sample prompts during the PoC.

4) Failover behavior
- Automatic cross-region failover is possible but only recommended for availability SLAs that accept temporary non-EU processing. For compliance-first customers we advise a manual or approval-gated failover process.

I've attached a short architecture diagram and will bring a checklist for the technical call (KMS, logging, KV retention, auditing).
